advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface a durable-read failure distinctly (e.g. an explicit durable-error marker) instead of silently omitting the 'durable' field, so a caller can tell 'checked and no attestation' from 'the durable check itself failed'.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:113-115: `except Exception: logger.warning(...); return None` swallows all errors
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:161-163: `durable = _durable_verdict(...); if durable is not None: out["durable"] = durable` — a None durable is silently dropped

docstring src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py: `durable` ... "so a caller can confirm the verdict actually persisted"
advisory.finding: gate_run_status omits the 'durable' field on any exception from the durable-verdict read (the exception is swallowed and logged, returning None), and since plan_review_status/verify_completion_status always return a dict (never None) an absent 'durable' means only 'the read errored'. A caller told the field lets them 'confirm the verdict actually persisted' cannot distinguish 'durable read failed' from a normal shape — the failure of the persistence check is invisible.
scenarios: A durable read raises (e.g. a signing/store read error); gate_status returns a normal-looking record with no 'durable' field, and a caller polling for persistence sees only silent absence.

A follower's client that polls gate_status(job_id) before the leader daemon's index write lands reads 'unknown' for a job that is genuinely in flight, momentarily indistinguishable from a bad job_id.

ABSENCE: no test polls a forced or REBAR_MCP_DEDUP=0 async run to stale-running (tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py only tests begin_gate_job attach/force and manually-recorded index entries)
blocking.finding: A forced (force=True) or dedup-disabled (REBAR_MCP_DEDUP=0) async gate start produces a GateJobHandle with no singleflight registry entry, so is_job_active(job_id) is always False for that run; because the daemon runs 15-20 minutes but the stale grace window is only 5s, gate_status reports a healthy, actively-running forced/bypassed run as 'stale-running' (a false crash signal) for essentially its entire duration.
scenarios: An agent calls review_plan_start(force=True) for a long review and polls gate_status(job_id); after ~5s the poll reports 'stale-running' though the gate is running fine.
An operator sets REBAR_MCP_DEDUP=0 as a kill-switch; every async start then reports stale-running mid-run.
blocking.suggested_fix: Track daemon liveness for every async start (including forced/bypass) — e.g. record the spawned thread's id/ident or a separate live-jobs set that is_job_active consults — rather than deriving liveness solely from the singleflight registry, which force/kill-switch runs intentionally skip.
